question:
The problem involves scheduling the landing times of four aircraft (aircraft_0, aircraft_1, aircraft_2, aircraft_3) at an airport to minimize the total penalty costs associated with deviations from their earliest possible landing times while adhering to separation and timing constraints. Each aircraft has an earliest and latest possible landing time, and penalty costs for landing early or late. Aircraft_0 has an earliest time of 0 minutes, latest time of 37 minutes, early penalty of \$61 per minute, and late penalty of \$82 per minute. Aircraft_1 has an earliest time of 7 minutes, latest time of 67 minutes, early penalty of \$35 per minute, and late penalty of \$34 per minute. Aircraft_2 has an earliest time of 225 minutes, latest time of 285 minutes, early penalty of \$74 per minute, and late penalty of \$41 per minute. Aircraft_3 has an earliest time of 119 minutes, latest time of 179 minutes, early penalty of \$93 per minute, and late penalty of \$56 per minute.

The landing order between any two aircraft must be explicitly determined using binary decision variables, ensuring one lands before the other. Separation constraints are enforced based on these landing orders, with coefficients modifying the required separation time depending on the landing sequence. For example, if aircraft_0 lands before aircraft_1, the separation constraint is adjusted by coefficients such as 2 and 30 depending on the order. Similar adjustments apply to other pairs: aircraft_0 and aircraft_2, aircraft_0 and aircraft_3, aircraft_1 and aircraft_2, aircraft_1 and aircraft_3, and aircraft_2 and aircraft_3. These constraints ensure that the separation between consecutive landings is maintained according to the specific coefficients provided in the LP data.

Each aircraft must land within its specified earliest and latest possible landing times. Early deviations are calculated as the difference between the earliest time and the actual landing time if the aircraft lands early, and late deviations are calculated as the difference between the actual landing time and the earliest time if the aircraft lands late. The total penalty cost is the sum of the early and late penalties for all aircraft, weighted by their respective penalty rates. The objective is to determine the optimal landing times for all four aircraft to minimize the total penalty costs while ensuring all separation and timing constraints are satisfied.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement (and fixed modelling decisions).
DATA = {
    "aircraft": ["aircraft_0", "aircraft_1", "aircraft_2", "aircraft_3"],
    # earliest landing times (minutes)
    "earliest": {
        "aircraft_0": 0,
        "aircraft_1": 7,
        "aircraft_2": 225,
        "aircraft_3": 119,
    },
    # latest landing times (minutes)
    "latest": {
        "aircraft_0": 37,
        "aircraft_1": 67,
        "aircraft_2": 285,
        "aircraft_3": 179,
    },
    # early penalty per minute
    "early_penalty": {
        "aircraft_0": 61,
        "aircraft_1": 35,
        "aircraft_2": 74,
        "aircraft_3": 93,
    },
    # late penalty per minute
    "late_penalty": {
        "aircraft_0": 82,
        "aircraft_1": 34,
        "aircraft_2": 41,
        "aircraft_3": 56,
    },
    # separation coefficient: 2 when i lands before j, 30 when j lands before i
    # assumption: sep[(i,j)] = 2 when i lands before j, sep[(j,i)] = 30 (swapped orientation)
    "sep_forward": 2,
    "sep_backward": 30,
    # assumption: bigM = 1000 (text silent)
    "bigM": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    aircraft = d["aircraft"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of aircraft
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=aircraft)

    # Ordered pairs of distinct aircraft (i != j)
    model.P = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(i, j) for i in aircraft for j in aircraft if i != j],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # Landing time t_i: NonNegativeReals within [earliest, latest]
    # "Each aircraft has an earliest and latest possible landing time"
    model.t = pyo.Var(
        model.I,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, i: (d["earliest"][i], d["latest"][i]),
    )

    # Early deviation e_i: NonNegativeReals
    # "Early deviations are calculated as the difference between the earliest time
    #  and the actual landing time if the aircraft lands early"
    model.e = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Late deviation l_i: NonNegativeReals
    # "late deviations are calculated as the difference between the actual landing
    #  time and the earliest time if the aircraft lands late"
    model.l = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Order variable y[i,j] Binary for all ordered pairs i != j
    # "The landing order between any two aircraft must be explicitly determined
    #  using binary decision variables, ensuring one lands before the other."
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total weighted early + late penalty costs
    # "The total penalty cost is the sum of the early and late penalties for all
    #  aircraft, weighted by their respective penalty rates."
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["early_penalty"][i] * m.e[i] + d["late_penalty"][i] * m.l[i]
            for i in aircraft
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Time link equality: t_i = earliest_i - e_i + l_i
    # "Early deviations are calculated as the difference between the earliest time
    #  and the actual landing time if the aircraft lands early, and late deviations
    #  are calculated as the difference between the actual landing time and the
    #  earliest time if the aircraft lands late."
    def link_rule(m, i):
        return m.t[i] == d["earliest"][i] - m.e[i] + m.l[i]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=link_rule)

    # Exactly one of y[i,j], y[j,i] is active (one lands before the other)
    # "ensuring one lands before the other"
    def order_rule(m, i, j):
        if aircraft.index(i) < aircraft.index(j):
            return m.y[i, j] + m.y[j, i] == 1
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.order = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=order_rule)

    # Separation constraints with big-M linearisation.
    # If i lands before j (y[i,j] = 1): t_j >= t_i + sep_forward
    # If j lands before i (y[i,j] = 0): t_j >= t_i - sep_backward (relaxed via bigM)
    # "Separation constraints are enforced based on these landing orders, with
    #  coefficients modifying the required separation time depending on the
    #  landing sequence."
    def sep_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.t[j] >= m.t[i] + d["sep_forward"] - d["bigM"] * (1 - m.y[i, j])

    model.sep = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=sep_rule)

    return model
